items.title: Qwen released giant open weights
items.oneliner: Qwen dropped 2.4T open weights with 95B active parameters, but local use is fantasy for almost everyone.

items.title: Grok 4.6 pushed agent models forward
items.oneliner: xAI says Grok 4.6 hits 61 on Intelligence Index and cuts prices 60%, raising the floor for agent workloads.

items.title: DeepSeek undercut the frontier again
items.oneliner: DeepSeek V4 Pro landed at $0.435 input and $0.87 output per million tokens, making premium inference harder to justify.

items.title: Microsoft shipped its first reasoning model
items.oneliner: Microsoft unveiled MAI-Thinking-1 as its first in-house reasoning model, signaling less dependence on external frontier labs.

items.title: SQLite exposed a 16-year bug
items.oneliner: Tailscale traced 19 corruption events to a 16-year-old SQLite WAL-reset bug, a reminder that boring infra still bites.

items.title: Facebook effectively beat ad blockers
items.oneliner: uBlock Origin stopped chasing Facebook ads, which tells you how hostile closed platforms have become to user-side control.

items.title: Google put sign language into Pixel
items.oneliner: Google's SL2T lets Deaf users sign ASL into Pixel 11, showing multimodal AI finally shipping as accessibility infrastructure.

items.title: Zed introduced collaborative agent coding
items.oneliner: Zed's Delta records code and conversation together, which could make agent-driven edits auditable instead of mysteriously generated.

items.title: OpenAI finally acknowledged Linux developers
items.oneliner: OpenAI opened ChatGPT Desktop signups for Linux, closing an obvious platform gap for serious developer adoption.

items.title: Flutter decoupled its design system
items.oneliner: Flutter 3.47 split Material and Cupertino into standalone packages, a quiet architectural change that should speed framework evolution.
